paper_metadata.title: Phenotyping juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. Praxis induction as a biomarker of unfavorable prognosis

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (Praxis Induction) was rigorously defined using both patient self-report and objective confirmation via a standardized video-EEG neuropsychological protocol.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: PI... is defined as precipitation of seizures or epileptiform discharges (ED) by complex, cognition-guided tasks, often involving visuomotor coordination and decision making
items.reasoning: The study provides a clear conceptual and operational definition of Praxis Induction.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: PI was ascertained if at least one NPP task produced myoclonic seizures or ED activation (defined as ED per minute during NPP task at least the double of that in baseline EEG)
items.reasoning: The use of video-EEG with a specific neuropsychological protocol (NPP) and quantitative ED criteria ensures high reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: defined as ED per minute during NPP task at least the double of that in baseline EEG
items.reasoning: The cut-point for ED activation is based on established literature (Matsuoka/Mayer/Wolf) rather than being data-driven by this specific study.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: all 133 consecutive patients had a 4–6 h video-EEG monitoring... NPP, composed by tasks such as reading silently and aloud, talking, writing...
items.reasoning: All patients underwent the same standardized protocol.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Group 1—JME with PI reported on questionnaire and confirmed by video-EEG NPP... and Group 2—JME without any reflex epileptic trait
items.reasoning: The PF status was confirmed for all included patients.

items.label: Method used for missing data

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: Imputation was not required as PF status was a prerequisite for group assignment.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes rely on seizure diaries and clinical interviews, which are standard but subject to patient recall bias. However, the long follow-up and use of standardized calendars mitigate this.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Myoclonia and absences were quantified as seizure days per month... GTCS frequency currently was the sum of all seizures occurred over the last year of follow-up.
items.reasoning: The outcomes (seizure frequency and freedom) are clearly defined for each seizure type.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Standard seizure calendars monitored seizure frequency.
items.reasoning: Seizure calendars are standard but rely on patient reporting. There is no mention of blinding the clinicians assessing the diaries to the PI status.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients were followed-up for one to 15 years (mean 7.82 years; SD = 3.98).
items.reasoning: The follow-up and measurement methods (calendars/interviews) were consistent across both groups.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study measures key confounders like psychiatric comorbidities and treatment types. However, it does not use a multivariable model to adjust for all these factors simultaneously when assessing the primary outcome of seizure freedom.

items.evidence_snippet: Psychiatric comorbidity was then analyzed through Schedule Clinical Interview for DSM-IV... AED therapy and treatment adherence were observed.
items.reasoning: Key confounders in JME (psychiatric issues, medication adherence, and treatment type) were measured.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

items.reasoning: While multivariate regression was used to identify factors associated with PI, it is not clearly stated that the final prognosis (seizure freedom) was adjusted for all confounders in a single model.
